claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can initially exist as a high-temperature, single-phase BCC microstructure.
Phase stability in high-temperature BCC Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by competition between the BCC-to-competing-phase Gibbs free-energy difference and kinetic barriers to atomic reconfiguration.
Cooling increases the thermodynamic instability of BCC Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 relative to FCC or other low-temperature phases.
A sufficiently large thermodynamic driving force can overcome kinetic hindrances and trigger a phase transformation during cooling.
Small changes around 7 at% Al alter the Gibbs free-energy difference between BCC and competing phases.
Small changes around 7 at% Al alter transformation kinetics.
The BCC-to-competing-phase Gibbs free-energy difference drives nucleation and growth of a new phase.
Atomic diffusivity governs the transformation rate.
At high temperature, the BCC phase is metastable.
At high temperature, limited diffusion suppresses transformation of the metastable BCC phase.
On cooling, ΔGbcc–competing phase becomes increasingly negative because of composition-dependent thermodynamic instability.
Transformation starts when the thermodynamic driving force surpasses a kinetic barrier.
Transformation onset occurs when the calculated ΔGbcc–competing phase reaches a critical value.
During cooling, the BCC phase will persist to a specific lower temperature and then a new phase such as FCC will nucleate and grow.
Minor changes in Al content will shift the transformation-onset temperature systematically and predictably.
The proposed mechanism applies only where diffusion remains sufficient for transformation and may fail when oxidation, grain-boundary effects, or non-equilibrium cooling dominate.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes an increasing ΔGbcc–competing phase as favoring the competing phase, whereas the mechanism says ΔGbcc–competing phase becomes increasingly negative to favor that phase. These statements use incompatible directions for the same free-energy quantity unless its sign convention is redefined.
The initial and boundary descriptions call the high-temperature BCC regime stable, while the mechanism calls the high-temperature BCC phase metastable.
